headline: Man Has Been Replying to Same Threadit Post for 11 Years Waiting for OP
subheadline: Original poster last active in 2013; devoted replier remains 'cautiously optimistic'
summary: A Threadit user has maintained an 11-year vigil in a single thread, waiting for a response that may never come.
content:
Threadit user u/StillWaiting has been replying to the same thread for 11 years, checking in daily with updates while waiting for the original poster to return.

The thread, titled "Quick question about Python—will check back for answers," was posted in 2013 by u/PythonNewbie, who asked for help with a coding problem and never returned. u/StillWaiting answered the question within hours. They have been maintaining the thread ever since.

"Day 4,017," reads the most recent reply. "OP still hasn't confirmed if the solution worked. Weather here is nice. Hope you're doing well, wherever you are."

The replies form a remarkable document: over 4,000 daily check-ins spanning more than a decade. They include life updates, weather reports, and occasional re-explanations of the original Python solution "in case OP needs it refreshed."

"I got married since I first posted," reads one entry from 2019. "Wife understands about the thread. She's supportive. Still no word from OP."

When reached for comment via Threadit message, u/StillWaiting explained their dedication: "I gave an answer. They said they'd check back. I believe in following through. They might come back any day. I want to be here when they do."

The thread has become a landmark in the Threadit community. Other users have begun leaving their own replies, some encouraging u/StillWaiting, others expressing concern.

"This is either the most beautiful or most concerning thing I've ever seen on the internet," commented one user. It received 847 upvotes.

u/PythonNewbie's account shows last activity in November 2013. The Python question they asked is now outdated—the solution would be different in modern versions. u/StillWaiting has updated their answer accordingly, "just in case."

"I'll keep waiting," they said. "That's the deal. That's what I signed up for."
author: Marcus Webb, Internet Culture Correspondent
